p:cNvPr.descr: A diagram showing conversion between NAD+ and NADH. NAD+, on the lower left, is oriented vertically and consists of 2 pentose rings, oriented vertically relative to each other, bonded on the left by 2 phosphate groups. The pentose ring has an O at the top, which bonds down and right to C, which bonds up and right to adenine, down to H, and down and left to C, which bonds up to H and down to OH, and left to C which also bonds up to H and down to OH. C bonds up and left to C, which bonds up and right to O, down to H, and up to CH2. CH2 bonds left to O, which bonds up to P, which bonds right to O-, double bonds left to O, and bonds up to O. O bonds up to the P of the second phosphate group, which is identical to the one just described. The top O of the phosphate group bonds right to the CH2 of the second pentose ring. The adenine bonded to the right side of the bottom pentose ring. It is shaded orange, and consists of a 5-sided ring and a 6-sided ring. The 5-sided ring is on the left and begins with the N that bonds up from the C of the pentose ring. N bonds up and left to C, which double bonds up and right to N. N bonds right to C, which double bonds down to C and left to N. To the right is the 6-sided ring. Its bottom N bonds up and right to C, which double bonds up to C, which double bonds up and right to C. C bonds up to NH2, which double bonds down and right to N. N bonds down to C, which double bonds down and left to N. Bonded to the top pentose ring, on the right side, is a pink section of the molecule consisting of one 6-sided ring. The ring consists of an N+ on the bottom, which double bonds up and left to C. C bonds up to C, which double bonds up and right to C, which bonds up to H and down and right to C. C double bonds up and right to C, which double bonds up to O and down and right to NH2. C double bonds down to C, which bonds down and left to N. To the right is a right arrow with 2 convergent arrows at the top and bottom. The top arrow is labeled 2e- indicating the addition of 2 electrons; the bottom arrow is labeled 2H+ in blue, indicating their addition as well. To the right of this are two possible pink structures for NADH (reduced), labeled below. The leftmost structure is a 6-sided ring. Its bottom N has 2 pink dots above it, representing electrons. The N bonds down to a black R group, bonds up and left to C, which double bonds up to C. C bonds up and right to C, which solid wedge bonds up and left to H and dashed wedge bonds up and right to H, but the H is blue, from the protonation on the arrow mentioned earlier. That C below it bonds down and right to C, which bonds up and right to C, which double bonds up to O and down and right to CH2. The C of the ring double bonds down to C, which bonds down and left to the initial N. To the right of the structure is the word “or” indicating the other possible structure to the right. The structure is identical to the one just described, but to the right it has a + sign, and to the right of that, a blue H+.
